verdict: NOT READY: fix the four confirmed findings before relying on partnerships for commercial combo sales.
scope: Existing partnership lifecycle and connected combo offer behavior; ordinary concurrent operator usage, not a load test.
method: Invitation creation and re-invitation used the real repository handler with real authentication and the production database; the email transport alone was intercepted. Acceptance, revocation, partner-tour reads, tenant denial, read-only denial and email-link behavior used deployed HTTP endpoints. Claire’s account is read-only; its mutation was correctly denied, and platform Super Admin targeting Claire was used for recipient acceptance. Test sessions were signed out locally afterwards.

findings.title: The inviting operator can accept without the partner’s consent
findings.what: Accept should activate an invitation only when the receiving operator agrees.
findings.problem: A live Kayak request accepting its own outgoing invitation returned HTTP 200 and changed the database status to ACTIVE. Listing pending partnerships also returns invite_token and invite_email to the sender, allowing the unauthenticated token acceptance route to be used as a second bypass.
findings.fix: Restrict dashboard acceptance to the receiving operator; omit invitation tokens from dashboard and creation responses; clear the token on every successful acceptance.
findings.impact: An operator can establish a commercial partnership and build offers without the other operator agreeing.
findings.proof: Live HTTP API and persisted database row.

findings.title: Revoking a partnership does not reliably stop its combo offers
findings.what: Revocation promises to deactivate all combo offers between the operators.
findings.problem: An offer containing three tours across two operators has no legacy partnership_id, so the revoke query misses it. Even a two-tour offer that is deactivated can immediately be activated again: activation checks offer participation but not an active partnership. Checkout checks active offers without checking the partnership.
findings.fix: Resolve affected offers through combo_offer_items as well as the legacy partnership_id; require active partnerships on activation and checkout; apply revocation and offer deactivation atomically.
findings.impact: Customers can continue buying joint offers after an operator has ended the partnership.
findings.proof: Isolated executions of the actual route handlers with synthetic offer rows; checkout code traced. No public test offers or customer purchases created.

findings.title: A revoked pair cannot be invited again
findings.what: An operator should be able to send a fresh invitation after a partnership has been revoked.
findings.problem: The existing-row check ignores REVOKED rows, then tries to insert the same operator pair again. The database rejects it with the unique_partnership constraint and the route returns HTTP 500.
findings.fix: Reuse the revoked pair with a conditional update to PENDING, a fresh invitation token, and cleared acceptance/revocation timestamps. Keep concurrent active or pending invitations protected.
findings.impact: Operators need manual database repair to partner again.
findings.proof: Repository invite handler, real authenticated Kayak session, real Supabase database; only email delivery intercepted.

findings.title: Opening an email link accepts immediately
findings.what: The emailed invitation URL is a GET endpoint that changes partnership status.
findings.problem: An unauthenticated GET changed a pending test invitation to ACTIVE without a confirmation step. Email security scanners and previews can request such URLs before the recipient chooses to accept; that unintended acceptance is a risk inferred from the confirmed GET mutation.
findings.fix: Make GET display an escaped confirmation page without writes; accept through an explicit POST with recipient verification, an atomic pending-state check, and token consumption.
findings.impact: A scanner or preview can accept on the recipient’s behalf. The current GET also bypasses the email proof required by accept_token POST.
findings.proof: Live unauthenticated GET and persisted database row; replay correctly returned HTTP 404.

not_checked: Actual invitation email delivery (intercepted for fake invites).
